hook: Alonzo Church was born in Washington, D.C., in 1903 and earned his doctorate in mathematics at Princeton in 1927 under Oswald Veblen. Returning to Princeton as a professor, he spent the early 1930s building a formal system, the lambda calculus, for defining functions purely through variable binding and substitution. In 1936 he used it to prove that no general algorithm can decide whether an arbitrary mathematical statement is provable, a result paired with Alan Turing's independent proof the same year into what is now called the Church-Turing thesis. He founded the Journal of Symbolic Logic and, over four decades at Princeton and later UCLA, supervised more than thirty doctoral students, including Alan Turing, Stephen Kleene, and Michael Rabin. The lambda calculus he built to answer a question in mathematical logic became, decades later, the theoretical foundation of Lisp and every later functional programming language.

quick_facts: Earned his Ph.D. in mathematics from Princeton University in 1927 under Oswald Veblen
Introduced the lambda calculus in the early 1930s as a formal system for defining and combining functions
Proved in 1936, in An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory, that no algorithm can decide general provability
Founded the Journal of Symbolic Logic in 1936 and edited it for decades
Supervised more than thirty doctoral students at Princeton and UCLA, including Alan Turing and Stephen Kleene
Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1978

achievements.title: Lambda calculus (early 1930s)
achievements.impact: Built a formal notation for defining functions by variable binding and substitution alone. It later became the theoretical foundation of Lisp and every subsequent functional programming language.

achievements.title: An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory (1936)
achievements.impact: Proved the Entscheidungsproblem has no general algorithmic solution, establishing that some questions in mathematics have no computational answer at all.

achievements.title: The Church-Turing thesis
achievements.impact: His result, combined independently with Alan Turing's 1936 proof, produced the working definition of computability that computer science still uses.

achievements.title: Doctoral advising at Princeton and UCLA (1929-1990)
achievements.impact: Trained a generation of logicians and computer scientists, including Alan Turing, Stephen Kleene, and Michael Rabin, who carried computability theory into computer science.
